title: Reduced integral exchange is the image of finite etale exchange
statement: Use O_E,A and the derived scalar functors of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. Fix prime ℓ, a finite normed extension E/ℚ_ℓ, a field k of positive prime characteristic different from ℓ, separated finite-type k-schemes X,Y,X′,Y′ and morphisms over k forming any commutative square g′;f=f′;g. For every bounded constructible integral complex M on X there are a functor F from the bounded-below derived category of etale sheaves of ULift A-modules on Y′ to the full derived category of internal continuous A-module objects on Y′, and a bounded-below etale complex L on X, such that derived reduction of the specified boundedConstructibleBaseChange component at M and F applied to the specified etale baseChange component at L are isomorphic as arrows. There is no properness or Cartesian assumption, and no assertion that either arrow is invertible.

source.place: Sections 5.4, 6.5 (especially Lemma 6.5.11) and 6.8, finite coefficient realization and exchange compatibility

proof.text: The quotient A is finite and discrete by the coefficient construction. Identify its pulled condensed continuous-function ring with the constant A sheaf. Restrict and extend the scalar action to identify internal modules over this ring with sheaves of A-modules, without changing underlying abelian sheaves or maps. These constructions are inverse exact equivalences and induce functors of derived categories.
Derived reduction of M has bounded constructible finite cohomology. Finite coefficient derived origin gives an etale bounded-below complex L whose pro-etale inverse image realizes that reduction.

Use the proved integralModuleReductionSequence_shortExact and exact monoidal inverse image from the profinite point to construct the two-term coefficient resolution in internal modules. Derived reduction commutes with pullback by tensor associativity. It commutes with the relevant direct images because A has the two-term finite free resolution O_E --ℓ--> O_E and direct image preserves finite distinguished triangles. Compare the units and counits before deriving; bounded-below site comparison identifies direct images of etale-origin objects. This gives the object comparisons on both ends of the exchange arrows.

Take F to be the inverse-image derived functor followed by the exact internal-module realization on Y′. Substitute the preceding comparisons into the unit, square, counit formula for baseChange. Naturality and the triangular identities prove the commuting square; the two endpoint comparisons are invertible, giving the displayed Arrow isomorphism. No proper base-change theorem is used in this construction.

theorem integralFiniteExchange_comparison
    (sq : CommSq g' f' f g)
    (M : integralConstructible ℓ E X) :
    ∃ (F : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf Y'.smallEtaleTopology
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (integralResidue ℓ E)))) ⥤
        integralResidueDerived ℓ E Y')
      (L : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (integralResidue ℓ E))))),
      Nonempty (Arrow.mk ((integralReduction ℓ E Y').map
          ((boundedConstructibleBaseChange (integralCoeff ℓ E) ℓ k sq).app M).hom) ≅
        Arrow.mk (F.map ((Etale.baseChange
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (integralResidue ℓ E))) sq).app L)))
